medicina.titulo: In a first, ultrasound maps blood flow through an entire human kidney in 3D
medicina.resumo: For the first time, a research team at the Inserm Institute of Physics for Medicine (Inserm/ESPCI Paris-PSL/CNRS) in Paris has succeeded in visualizing the entire vascular network and blood flow in a human kidney. This breakthrough opens up promising clinical prospects: improving our understanding and diagnosis of kidney diseases linked to vascular defects. To achieve this, the researchers used a new ultrasound technique developed in their laboratory and previously tested in animals, which could eventually be extended to other organs. The results are published in The Lancet Medical Imaging & Theranostics.

medicina.titulo: New approach could make curative lung cancer treatment possible for more patients
medicina.resumo: Despite significant advances in treatment, lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. A clinical trial recently published in Nature Medicine suggests that a more flexible approach to treating locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer could open up new treatment options for patients. By starting with a combination of chemotherapy and immunotherapy (durvalumab), followed by reassessment by a multidisciplinary team, doctors may be able to offer curative surgery to more patients. The study also suggests that patients who remain ineligible for surgery after this initial treatment may still have another potentially curative option: a combination of chemotherapy and radiation therapy.

biologia.titulo: Why fertile male killifish outlive their peers
biologia.resumo: Why do some individuals of the same species live significantly longer than others? In evolutionary biology and aging research, this question is often linked to a trade-off between reproduction and survival. The underlying idea is that energy and resources invested in reproduction may lead to compromises in repair and maintenance, thereby hindering a long life. Thus, the assumption is that particularly successful reproduction at a young age comes at the cost of a shorter lifespan.

biologia.titulo: Protein redesign boosts DNA insertion activity and reveals how molecular machinery selects targets
biologia.resumo: Genome engineering is exciting, given its vast potential to treat and even cure diseases, but it is still a largely uncharted biomedical innovation. Scientists at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital recently uncovered the mechanisms involved in precisely integrating DNA into a target genomic location using CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs). By studying type I-F3 CAST, the researchers unveiled structural findings that explain how this CAST family achieves successful DNA integration at precise target sites and offer insights for future genomic engineering approaches. The results were published in Nature.

biologia.titulo: New fern species discovered after nearly 200 years of being mistaken for another
biologia.resumo: Chinese researchers have formally described a new fern species that has been hiding in plain sight for nearly 200 years. Named Drynaria lineatisora, the species was collected as early as the 19th century in Myanmar and Vietnam, but it was repeatedly misidentified as the widespread Drynaria coronans. Recent field studies by researchers from the Xishuangbanna Tropical Botanical Garden (XTBG) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and their collaborators confirmed that it is indeed a distinct species.

biologia.titulo: Researchers reveal sex chromosome evolution and molecular sex markers in the pitcher plant Nepenthes mirabilis
biologia.resumo: Researchers have uncovered the genomic basis of sex determination in Nepenthes mirabilis, the only pitcher plant native to China, identifying an XX/XY sex chromosome system and molecular markers that can distinguish male from female plants long before they flower.

Netflix is also exploring agent-assisted consumer migrations. By Leela Kumili

astrofisica.titulo: A small galaxy's giant dark matter core challenges the standard cosmological model
astrofisica.resumo: New findings show that a nearby dwarf galaxy, UGCA 320, may challenge some predictions of the widely accepted cosmological model of the universe. By combining observations from the MUSE instrument with radio measurements from the MeerKAT telescope, astronomers have found that it hosts an unusually large dark matter core. The paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Nov. 11.

astrofisica.titulo: The dark matter puzzle deepens: Nearby galaxies challenge cosmic simulations
astrofisica.resumo: Galaxies appear to hold a surprise beneath their visible stars: Their inner regions contain less dark matter than some of our most advanced simulations predict. Dark matter is invisible, but its gravitational pull helps govern the motions of stars and gas. By measuring these movements, astronomers can reconstruct where this unseen matter lies and test the computer simulations used to understand the universe. A study of 136 nearby galaxies, involving the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC), reveals a discrepancy that becomes more extensive in more massive systems, offering fresh clues about how galaxies form and evolve.

astrofisica.titulo: The faintest supernova ever observed refuses to go out, staying visible for nearly a year
astrofisica.resumo: An international team of astronomers, including Paul Groot of Radboud University, has discovered that a supernova explosion does not always have to be extremely bright. The team has identified the faintest supernova observed to date. It remained visible for an exceptionally long time and appears to have been caused by a so-called white dwarf and a relatively small companion star. The discovery may have implications for our understanding of the evolution of binary stars and the measurement of the expansion of the universe. The results were published in Nature Astronomy.

astrofisica.titulo: JWST studies a tiny, metal-poor galaxy with just a fraction of the sun's oxygen abundance
astrofisica.resumo: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) have studied one of the most metal-poor galaxies known. Seen as it was around 12.2 billion years ago, LAP2 is a tiny system with a stellar mass comparable to that of a massive star cluster. The research paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Nov. 3.

While he was trained as an emergency physician, he had also taught himself to code just before entering medical school. After completing a fellowship in clinical informatics—which focuses on the intersection of clinical practice and IT systems—he moved into health technology. inteligencia_artificial.resumo: Gemini Live vai ganhar aba de Atividade para gerenciar tarefas e rotinas da IA O Google trabalha em uma atualização para o Gemini Live que permitirá acompanhar tarefas executadas pela inteligência artificial (IA) em segundo plano . O modo de conversas por voz do Gemini ganhará uma seção chamada "Atividade", que reunirá tarefas pontuais e programadas pelo usuário. A novidade foi identificada pelo portal Android Authority nesta sexta-feira (27), durante uma análise do código da versão 17.78.14 do aplicativo do Google para Android. Atualmente, já é possível solicitar a execução de tarefas por meio do Gemini Live. A atualização permitirá acompanhar essas atividades sem precisar retornar à interface principal do aplicativo. Como funcionará a aba de Atividade do Gemini Live? Localizada na parte superior da interface do Gemini Live, a nova seção será dividida em duas categorias: Tarefas: atividades atribuídas à IA para serem executadas em segundo plano; Agendadas: tarefas que devem ser realizadas periodicamente, conforme as instruções do usuário. energia_materiais.titulo: Salty lake water helps a zinc battery keep working at −50°C
energia_materiais.resumo: Extreme cold can affect a water-based battery's ability to deliver electricity. Its liquid electrolyte—the fluid that carries charge—can freeze, while the charged particles moving through it slow down. Researchers have now built a rechargeable zinc battery that works at −50°C (−58°F) using saline lake water as a starting ingredient.

energia_materiais.titulo: CNH B pode dirigir eletrificados com mais de 4.250 kg?
energia_materiais.resumo: CNH B pode dirigir eletrificados com mais de 4.250 kg? Quem dirige SUVs e picapes eletrificados precisa ter atenção. É que esses carros podem ser mais pesados que suas versões equivalentes a combustão — e, graças a uma mudança no Código de Trânsito Brasileiro (CTB) sancionada em setembro, motoristas com CNH na categoria B foram autorizados a conduzir elétricos ou híbridos com peso bruto total (PBT) de até 4.250 kg . A alteração no CTB importa porque amplia em 750 kg o teto tradicional de 3.500 kg para compensar o peso extra das baterias presentes em SUVs e picapes eletrificados — contanto que o modelo possua tração predominantemente elétrica. A flexibilização foi incorporada a uma legislação voltada a linhas de financiamento para taxistas, transporte escolar e motoristas de aplicativo, mas beneficia todos os condutores da categoria B que respeitarem o limite de até oito lugares além do motorista. Para modelos puramente a combustão ou sem predominância elétrica, o limite máximo de 3.500 kg permanece. energia_materiais.resumo: Virginia Tech scientists have discovered how to transform one of the world's hardest-to-recycle plastics into a valuable ingredient for high-performance engine oil. Their innovative process converts discarded PVC into a useful lubricant material in just three hours. The breakthrough could turn a major source of plastic pollution into a valuable industrial resource while making lubricant production more sustainable.

ciberseguranca.titulo: Extensão falsa do Planilhas Google é usada para espionar e roubar e-mails do Gmail
ciberseguranca.resumo: Extensão falsa do Planilhas Google é usada para espionar e roubar e-mails do Gmail Uma extensão falsa do Planilhas Google (Google Sheets) está sendo utilizada por cibercriminosos para espionar e roubar e-mails do Gmail . A ferramenta maliciosa consegue monitorar até dez contas simultaneamente e pode voltar a interceptar mensagens mesmo após o usuário alterar sua senha. O ataque foi detalhado nesta terça-feira (24) por pesquisadores da empresa de cibersegurança Gen Threat Labs. A extensão é instalada no Google Chrome sem o conhecimento da vítima pelo Remus Stealer, um malware desenvolvido para roubar informações de usuários do Windows. Os responsáveis pelo malware afirmavam ter descoberto uma vulnerabilidade no Gmail. Em resposta ao portal Cybernews, o Google negou a existência de uma falha de segurança relacionada ao ataque. Como funciona o roubo de e-mails do Gmail? Após infectar o computador, o Remus modifica as configurações do Chrome para instalar a extensão e ativar o modo de desenvolvedor do navegador. A ferramenta aparece com o nome "Google Sheets" , na versão 0.5.4, e utiliza a descrição de uma extensão legítima do Google que permite editar documentos offline. A cada minuto

A fabricante chinesa estaria desenvolvendo um celular com três câmeras traseiras de 200 MP , incluindo uma lente ultrawide com sensor de grandes dimensões. As informações foram publicadas pelo leaker Digital Chat Station em uma postagem na rede social chinesa Weibo . A especificação sugere uma aposta em fotografias com ângulo mais amplo sem abrir mão de uma quantidade elevada de detalhes. Nova câmera ultrawide pode melhorar fotos noturnas A escolha de um sensor maior para a câmera ultrawide pode trazer benefícios que vão além da resolução do novo dispositivo da HONOR.
